ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: This quarter’s missed opportunity is overwhelmingly a rank problem, not budget: the three non-brand search campaigns sit at 5–7% search impression share while losing 93–95% to rank with 0% lost to budget, and auction data shows competitors consistently take top-of-page placements (your top-of-page rate 15.2% vs competitors 73.2%) even when you appear. Profitability is also pressured by low-intent/low-quality queries absorbing spend (e.g., QS 3.0 keyword spending 2,670.30 with 606.89 cost/conv), so simply bidding up without tightening intent and improving relevance would scale inefficiently.
notable_patterns: Non-brand demand is largely un-captured due to rank: Non-Brand Auto IS 6% with 94% lost to rank (0% to budget); Home IS 5% with 95% lost to rank; Life IS 7% with 93% lost to rank, all with only ~52–58% budget utilization.

Competitors dominate the premium real estate: avg position-above-rate 85.4% and your avg top-of-page rate 15.2% vs competitors 73.2% (e.g., Nordkreuz Assurance position-above 96.5% with competitor top-of-page 82.6% vs your 17.1%).

There are “should win” keywords (high QS) still stuck at ~5–7% IS and ~93–95% lost rank: e.g., 'auto insurance germany' QS 9.0 at 5.0% IS (95% lost rank) and 'home insurance cost' QS 8.5 at 5.5% IS (94.5% lost rank).

Wasted/low-intent spend is visible: 'insurance company phone number' QS 3.0 spent 2,670.30 at 606.89 cost/conv; 'what is life insurance' QS 4.5 spent 867.21 at 1,084.01 cost/conv. Also, 48.3% of search-term impressions come from zero-click competitor-brand terms (35,700 impressions) which is unlikely to be efficient capture.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Very low coverage (6% impression share) is driven by rank, not budget (94% lost to rank; 0% lost to budget) while efficiency is poor (ROAS 0.86) and avg QS is weak at 5.3—suggesting ad/landing relevance and/or bidding posture aren’t competitive against rivals who appear above you most of the time.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Split intent tiers (quote/buy vs research/jobs), push bids and/or target position for high-intent, high-QS terms, and cut/negate low-intent terms consuming spend; align ads/LPs to raise QS above ~7 on key clusters.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Coverage is similarly constrained by rank (5% impression share; 95% lost to rank; 0% lost to budget). Despite a stronger avg QS (7.1), ROAS is still 0.88, indicating the traffic mix/queries are not converting profitably even when you do win auctions.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Bid/position up selectively on purchase-intent home-insurance keywords while tightening match types and negatives to reduce claims-process/how-to traffic that drives higher CPAs; use dedicated ad/LP messaging for 'cost/quote' intent.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Life non-brand is under-serving demand due to rank (7% impression share; 93% lost to rank; 0% lost to budget) with weak avg QS (5.3) and the worst ROAS of the three (0.74), consistent with informational queries (e.g., 'what is life insurance') absorbing spend at very high cost per conversion.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Carve out education terms into separate lower-bid budgets (or negate) and concentrate coverage on comparison/quote intent; rebuild ad groups/ads for tighter life-insurance relevance to lift QS and win more auctions where it matters.

recommendation_cards.title: Aggressively fix non-brand rank on “should-win” high-QS quote terms (selective bid/position push)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Across the three non-brand search campaigns, impression share is only 5–7% while 93–95% is lost to rank (and 0% to budget). Even high-quality keywords are not clearing auctions: 'auto insurance germany' QS 9.0 has 5.0% IS with 95% lost rank; 'home insurance cost' QS 8.5 has 5.5% IS with 94.5% lost rank; 'car insurance quote' QS 8.0 sits at 6.0% IS (94% lost rank). Auction data corroborates weak ad rank at the page: your top-of-page rate is 15.2% vs competitors 73.2%, with position-above-rate averaging 85.4%.
recommended_steps: Create a dedicated high-intent segment (exact/phrase) for quote/comparison terms (e.g., 'car insurance quote', 'life insurance comparison') and raise bids/targets only on that segment until top-of-page rate materially improves.
Deprioritize broad coverage until rank is solved: move research-intent themes to separate ad groups/campaigns with lower bids so incremental spend goes to purchasable intent.
Benchmark progress weekly using top-of-page rate and lost-to-rank on the high-intent segment; keep scaling only if CPA/ROAS holds.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Top-of-page rate on non-brand rising from 15.2% toward ~30%+ while lost impression share (rank) on the high-intent segment drops meaningfully (e.g., from ~94% toward <70%).

recommendation_cards.title: Stop paying for low-intent/low-QS queries that are dragging ROAS (tighten intent with negatives + match restructuring)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Material spend is going to weak-intent terms with poor Quality Scores and extreme costs: 'insurance company phone number' (QS 3.0) spent 2,670.30 at 606.89 cost/conv; 'home insurance claims process' (QS 4.0) spent 2,257.65 at 217.08 cost/conv; 'what is life insurance' (QS 4.5) spent 867.21 at 1,084.01 cost/conv. Meanwhile, non-brand campaign ROAS is <1 (Auto 0.86, Home 0.88, Life 0.74), so removing these leaks is necessary before scaling bids to fix rank.
recommended_steps: Add/expand negatives for service/support intent (e.g., 'phone number', 'claims process') in the applicable non-brand campaigns; isolate any unavoidable support traffic into a separate campaign with capped bids.

Move high-CPA informational queries (e.g., 'what is life insurance') to a separate research ad group with lower bids and tailored educational landing, or negate if lead goals are strictly quote-focused.
Rebuild ad groups around tighter themes so QS is less exposed to mixed intent (aim to pull avg QS above ~7 on the main quote/comparison groups).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Cost per conversion on non-brand search dropping sharply (starting with eliminating the 606.89 and 1,084.01 CPA pockets) while non-brand ROAS moves from ~0.74–0.88 toward ≥1.0.

recommendation_cards.title: Eliminate competitor-brand zero-click waste (block or heavily down-bid competitor navigational terms)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: 48.3% of search-term impressions are coming from zero-click competitor-brand terms, totaling 35,700 impressions (e.g., 'bluewave insurance', 'harborline mutual', 'crestfield direct'), with only 1 recorded converting competitor-brand term shown ('nordkreuz insurance quote' with 1.0 conversion). Given your weak auction position overall (competitors’ top-of-page 73.2% vs your 15.2%), this traffic is likely expensive and low-yield relative to fixing non-brand quote intent.
recommended_steps: Add competitor brand names as negatives where competitor conquesting is not an explicit strategy; if conquesting is desired, isolate it into its own campaign/ad groups with strict bid caps and tailored ads.
Keep an exception for the one converting pattern by allowing only 'nordkreuz insurance quote' (or close variants) in an isolated test ad group, while blocking pure navigational variants.
Review search terms weekly to ensure competitor leakage share falls and does not re-emerge via close variants.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions from competitor zero-click terms falling from 48.3% toward <15% while maintaining (or improving) total conversions.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix self-blocking negative keyword conflicts that are suppressing coverage
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The negative-keyword conflicts report shows 3,810 estimated blocked impressions from your own negatives, including 'free' blocking 'insurance quote calculator free' in 'Dynamic Search Ads - Long Tail' (3,400 blocked impressions) and 'jobs' blocking 'insurance agent jobs near me insurance quote' in Non-Brand Auto (410 blocked impressions). While small versus the rank losses, these are direct, preventable blockers.
recommended_steps: Decide intent policy: if 'free' should only exclude bargain-hunters, add a more precise negative (e.g., 'free policy') and use a negative exception approach so calculator/quote tools can still serve if valuable.

For the 'jobs' conflict, keep 'jobs' as a negative but add the blocked query as an explicit negative phrase/exact if it’s recruiting-heavy; alternatively, route recruiting intent to a dedicated exclusions list shared across campaigns.
Re-run the conflicts report after changes to confirm blocked impressions drop toward zero.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Blocked impressions from conflicts decreasing from 3,810 toward 0, without an increase in irrelevant recruiting/support search terms.
